question: Which statement best describes Text values?
options: String methods such as `.toUpperCase()` return a changed string; they do not change the original. Save the result if the interface should display it. Language rules can affect capitalization and sorting, so use locale-aware APIs for names and text that depend on the user’s language. Formatting returns a new string. Store that result when it should be displayed, and use locale-sensitive APIs for language-specific casing or sorting. A string method is like making a marked-up copy while keeping the original note.

`.length` reports the number of UTF-16 code units, which may differ from the number of visible characters. A common emoji can occupy more than one code unit. For ordinary checks, length is useful; for product limits based on what people perceive as a character, use Unicode-aware segmentation. JavaScript counts UTF-16 code units, so some visible emoji count as more than one. Match the counting method to the user-facing requirement. String length is like counting marks on a page, not always the characters a reader sees.

A string is text and can use single quotes, double quotes, or backticks. For example, `"Hello"` and `'Hello'` both hold text. Choose a consistent quote style; use escapes when the text contains the same quote mark. Strings are immutable, so a method returns a new value rather than editing the original. Use a consistent quote convention so punctuation is easy to read. Escape a quote only when necessary, and avoid complex concatenation when a template literal is clearer. Quotation marks are like the edges of a note that show where its text begins and ends.

A template literal uses backticks and can insert an expression with `${...}`. For example, `` `Hello, ${name}` `` includes the current value of `name`. This is convenient for messages, but a template string does not escape HTML. If the value is user-controlled, insert it as text or use a safe framework rendering path. Interpolation inserts a value into text but does not make that value safe HTML. A framework’s text rendering or a safe DOM API should handle user-controlled content. A template literal is like filling a blank in a greeting card with a name.
